text:
Alex R: quick idea — let's pilot 4hr incident commander shifts for the next month. smaller handoffs, less fatigue. who thinks this is doable?
Maya S: hmm 4hr could help during busy windows. worried about more frequent knowledge gaps on handoff. need a tight checklist. :thinking_face:
Samir: +1 to shorter shifts for high-severity spikes. we should pair an IC with a 'follow-up owner' for 24h after incident closes. that owner owns remediations & comms until action item assigned.
Priya: can we try 4hr for the first 12 hours of an incident only? then revert to 8hr blocks at night. preserves continuity for low-activity windows.
Alex R: good call. proposal: 4hr for active incident windows (first 12h), then 8hr overnight. handoff cadence: IC -> IC (every 4h), IC -> follow-up-owner (at close).
Maya S: need a one-pager handoff template. short fields only so folks actually fill it.
Samir: draft template below — use this in the incident channel when handing off:
```
Handoff summary (1-2 lines):
Current state: [e.g., mitigating / recovered / partially degraded]
Top 3 actions in progress (owner, ETA):
Known risks / blockers:
Next IC check-in: [time UTC]
Follow-up owner: [name, pager]
Key logs / links: [incident doc, runbook, grafana panels]
```
Priya: love that. add a required field: 'unresolved alarms we expect to re-fire' — helps follow-up owners.
Alex R: communications cadence idea: short updates every 30m while escalation > P1, then hourly after steady-state. keep updates <2 lines unless new info. use :loudspeaker: channel thread.
Samir: agree. also add automated reminder to assign follow-up owner inside 2h of incident close. oncall-bot can nudge.
oncall-bot: Reminder queued — if incident status = closed and follow-up-owner not set, ping #eng-oncall after 2h.
Maya S: what about recurring pattern detection? we should tag incident types and run a weekly digest of similar incidents for product/infra owners.
Priya: yes — label with taxonomy: service, downstream, infra, infra-config, deploy, perf. weekly digest with top-3 recurring signals and suggested owners.
Samir: I'd like a lightweight tracker for postmortem actions — minimal fields: action id, owner, due date, status, severity, linked incident ts. expose as CSV via Google Sheet + a tiny bot that posts weekly reminders.
Alex R: we should also adopt an SLA for remediation closure: low/med/high severity -> 90/45/14 days? open to adjusting.
Maya S: suggest 60/30/10 to push critical fixes faster.
Priya: fine with Maya's numbers. add "micro-retro" 48h after major incidents: 20m async + 40m sync to confirm follow-ups and detect patterns.
Samir: action items:
- Alex: run pilot schedule doc + coordination with SRE (due in 3 days)
- Maya: produce one-page handoff template and Slack snippet (due 48h)
- Priya: implement taxonomy proposal for incident tags and weekly digest (due 1 week)
- Samir: build minimal CSV action tracker and oncall-bot reminders (due 1 week)
Alex R: sounds good. let's try pilot next Tuesday midday shift. :thumbsup:
Maya S: :thumbsup:
Priya: :thumbsup:
Samir: :thumbsup:
Alex R: I'll post a short sign-up sheet for IC slots and follow-up owners. if anyone wants to opt out of 4hr IC, ping me directly.
Maya S: one more thing — require a single line "why it's closed" when marking incident closed, helps follow-up owners triage.
Alex R: agreed. add to the close flow.
Priya: ok locking these items into the incident checklist. I'll update the runbook.
Samir: putting a calendar block to remind team leads about the weekly digest review.
Alex R: thanks everyone — great sync. we'll reconvene after the first pilot cycle and iterate.
